memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Maya made an explicitly trip-local exception to favoring Delta: although Delta was available and offered an earlier arrival, she retained Sun Country because Delta cost more after baggage and required a connection on the return.

messages.content: I have the three RSW flight combinations now. Compare the real timelines and costs for both of us, including one checked bag each. I also want the realistic arrival time in Naples, not just the RSW landing time.

Send me the departure and arrival times, carriers, connection points, and fare rules for each combination. I’ll put the baggage charges into the totals and measure them against the $4,800 flight-and-hotel ceiling, with airport transportation still shown separately.

Option one is Sun Country nonstop both ways for $1,086 total. Saturday is MSP 3:20 p.m. to RSW 7:45 p.m. Friday is RSW 1:15 p.m. to MSP 3:52 p.m. The fare is nonrefundable, with changes allowed for a fee plus any fare difference.

With one checked bag per person each way at $45 per bag, that becomes $1,266. Allowing about 20–30 minutes for bags and 45–55 minutes to Naples, you would likely reach the hotel around 8:55–9:20 p.m. Friday’s nonstop is straightforward and should put you home before 4:00 p.m.

Option two is American basic economy at $914 total. Saturday leaves MSP at 1:30 p.m., has 1 hour 3 minutes in Charlotte, and lands at RSW at 10:42 p.m. Friday leaves at 12:10 p.m., has 1 hour 26 minutes at DCA, and reaches MSP at 5:58 p.m.

American’s first checked bag is $40 each way, so the two-person total is $1,074. The outbound is about 8 hours 12 minutes overall. After collecting bags and driving south, hotel arrival would most likely be 11:50 p.m.–12:20 a.m. The connections are workable, but the Charlotte margin has little cushion if the first flight runs late. Basic economy is also the least flexible of the three fares.

The third is Delta at $1,174 total. It leaves MSP at 7:05 a.m. Saturday and lands nonstop at 11:30 a.m. The Friday return leaves RSW at 12:45 p.m., connects in Atlanta for 1 hour 8 minutes, and gets to MSP at 5:52 p.m. Main Cabin, changes without a fee but fare differences apply.

At $35 per checked bag each way, Delta comes to $1,314 for two. You would probably reach Naples around 12:35–1:00 p.m. Saturday, giving you most of the first day. The return is roughly 5 hours 7 minutes and the Atlanta connection is valid, though not generous. It has the best outbound timing and flexibility, but the highest bag-inclusive total and the only connection among the two more convenient choices.
Show me what each one leaves for the hotel, and then what remains if we also protect the high end of the RSW rideshare estimate.

Against the $4,800 flight-and-hotel ceiling, the bag-inclusive airfare leaves $3,534 with Sun Country, $3,726 with American, or $3,486 with Delta for six hotel nights. If we temporarily reserve $220 for airport rideshares as well, the practical lodging limits become $3,314, $3,506, and $3,266 respectively. That transportation reserve is still unbooked and separate from the paid-flight-and-hotel accounting.

American saves $192 from Sun Country, but arriving after midnight effectively wastes the first night and makes Saturday unpleasant. Delta buys us the beach afternoon, but it costs $48 more after bags and adds the Atlanta connection coming home.

That is the tradeoff. Sun Country is the middle-cost option, gets you to Naples in time for a late dinner, and keeps both directions nonstop. Delta creates roughly eight extra hours in Naples on Saturday, while American mainly serves the lowest-price case. If lodging comes in near $3,300, Sun Country also keeps the projected total near $4,786 using the $220 transportation reserve.

For this trip, don’t favor Delta. The early arrival is useful, but not enough to pay more and accept a return connection. Keep the Sun Country nonstops as the flight choice and use $3,300 all-in as the hotel target so we stay under the ceiling even with the larger rideshare estimate. Nothing should be booked yet.

Retained for planning: Sun Country nonstop round trip for two, August 25–31, at $1,086 before bags or $1,266 with one checked bag each way per traveler. Expected Naples arrival is about 8:55–9:20 p.m. Saturday. Use $3,300 all-in as the six-night hotel target; with $220 reserved for rideshares, the projected trip total is $4,786. The airfare, hotel, and transportation remain unbooked.
